summaries.demographer: Stanley Bates is a 47-year-old non-Hispanic White married man living in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, with his wife Megan and two teenage children, Evan and Claire (Q51, Q84, Q88, Q89). He was born in Royal Oak, grew up in Troy, and remains strongly rooted in metro Detroit (Q87, Q97). He has a bachelor's degree in computer information systems from Michigan State University and works as a salaried computer systems analyst with stable high household income (Q90, Q65, Q72, Q74). His household owns its home with a mortgage, has no lodgers or temporary members, and reports financial stability with savings and retirement planning (Q51-Q58, Q61, Q83).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Stanley shows strong planning behavior, automation of savings, budget tracking, and loss aversion around debt and lifestyle creep (Q57, Q61, Q63, Q83). He is willing to invest in long-term human capital through AWS and TOGAF certifications and in children's college savings, suggesting future-oriented time preferences (Q62, Q91, Q108). His decisions are pragmatic rather than status-driven: he chose technical leadership over a pure management title because it preserved learning, credibility, and family balance (Q02, Q03). He responds to uncertainty by building buffers, savings buckets, spreadsheets, and reliable routines (Q59-Q62, Q82).
summaries.political_scientist: Stanley is a regular voter who pays attention to local elections, school boards, library funding, infrastructure, and state races (Q23). He identifies as an Independent with a clear Democratic lean, describing himself as pragmatic center-left and concerned with competent government, public education, infrastructure, science, and fairness (Q24, Q95, Q96). His views on race and policing are reform-oriented but operationally cautious; he supports accountability, transparency, mental health response options, and listening to Black coworkers' lived experiences (Q26-Q30). He exhibits moderate institutional trust, especially in public health, schools, libraries, and local civic institutions (Q17, Q23, Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Stanley presents as calm, conscientious, curious, and systems-oriented, with a strong identity around reliability and usefulness (Q01, Q02, Q109). He regulates stress through exercise, garage work, cooking, photography, lists, and conversations with Megan, though he acknowledges overload during work incidents and elder-care stress (Q38, Q43-Q45, Q50). His self-concept combines technical competence with Midwestern service values learned from his manufacturing father and teacher mother (Q01, Q103-Q109). Relationally, he is family-centered, emotionally restrained but reflective, and increasingly intentional about apology, communication, and boundaries (Q05, Q44, Q46).
